boundary_condition: Apply only to flight seat-location selection; do not apply to cabin class, departure time, route choice, lodging, or other travel domains.
condition: When booking a flight and seat selection is available.
default_action: Request a window seat for the flight segment being booked.
exception_condition: If no window seat is available, or the user gives a conflicting seat priority such as accessibility needs, companion seating, or a different explicit seat location, do not force the window-seat default.
name: Prefer window seats on flights
rationale: Across independent flight task dialogues, users repeatedly ask for a window seat, often with availability language such as "if possible" or "if I can get one." Other details such as cabin class or departure time vary, so only the reusable window-seat preference is induced.

source_evidence.contribution: The user asks for "a window seat" on flights if possible, directly supporting the seat-location preference.
The user says they would like "a window seat" if they can get one, supporting a window-seat default with availability caveat.
The user states, "I would prefer a window seat," giving direct evidence for a reusable flight seat-location preference.
The user requests business class and says to "make sure" they get a window seat, supporting the concrete window-seat value independent of cabin class.
The user says, "Make sure that's a window seat if that's possible," reinforcing the window-seat default with an availability condition.

source_examples.user_utterance: Yeah. I'd like a window seat, too, if possible on both flights. That's it.
No. But I would like a window seat, if I can get one.
I would prefer a window seat and to leave in the morning. I would also prefer to be in coach.
I would like to travel business class and make sure that I get a window seat.
Okay. Make sure that's a window seat if that's possible.
